correctness.rationale: Pull an admissible output set back, after discarding zero coordinates. If the resulting nonempty set has minimum m and size s, then s≤m+n. Greedy blocks of capacities m, 2m, 4m, … are admissible because the rank of the first entry in a full-capacity block forces its index to be at least the block capacity. Their total capacity after l blocks is m(2^l−1), giving the ceiling upper bound. For the lower bound use p-th powers 1/(j+1) for 1≤j≤n+1: each admissible sum is at most the integral from m to 2m of dt/t, and all n+1 entries can be used together after translation. This works for n=0 and all real or complex 1≤p<∞. Density then extends the one-step operator and its powers. An eventually admissible shifted finite support yields the eventual ℓp norm; if a closed set of uniformly bounded orbits had interior, taking differences on a ball would bound all operator norms, contrary to the lower bound. This is a proof-level check; the frozen finite diagnostic was inspected, not executed or relied on.
